messages.subject: How to get the base information from Cel files
messages.subject_clean: How to get the base information from Cel files
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am not quite sure how to retrieve the information of SNP (single
base A, T, G, C) from the data. I know how to get the information from
the CDF files. However from CEL, how can I know what is the single
base?

  For example:

  SNP_XX  C/A (one Allele is C, one Allele is A),

  If the CEL file is xxx number for this SNP, how can I know the base
should be what?

 I know Genotyping Analysis can give me the call of  AA, AB, BB or No
calls with Affymetrix GTYPE software or Oligo package in R; AA means
CC for this example. But can that position be any other bases like G
or T?

Thanks and Best,

R

messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On Mon, Mar 31, 2008 at 7:00 PM, Racheal Zhang <rachea...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>  Hi,
>
>  I am not quite sure how to retrieve the information of SNP (single
>  base A, T, G, C) from the data. I know how to get the information from
>  the CDF files. However from CEL, how can I know what is the single
>  base?
>
>   For example:
>
>   SNP_XX  C/A (one Allele is C, one Allele is A),
>
>   If the CEL file is xxx number for this SNP, how can I know the base
>  should be what?
>
>   I know Genotyping Analysis can give me the call of  AA, AB, BB or No
>  calls with Affymetrix GTYPE software or Oligo package in R; AA means
>  CC for this example. But can that position be any other bases like G
>  or T?

I'm still not sure if I understand you what your question is.  It
would at least be useful to know what chip type you are using, since
Affymetrix have many different SNP chips.  Also, is you question
specific to the 'aroma.affymetrix' package, the 'affxparser' package
(as your first messages indicated), or just in general about
Affymetrix SNP chips?

A CEL file contains three fields: intensities, stdevs and pixels.  The
first two are the estimates of the average and the standard deviation
of all pixel intensities for each probe and the latter is the number
of pixels used in the probe.  There are no other probe or probeset
specific information in the CEL files.

There are tools that estimate/call the genotypes for each SNP.  As you
say, the typically calls are AA, AB, BB and NoCall (different tools
have slightly different kinds of NoCall calls).  Calling the two
alleles in bi-allelic SNPs A and B, respectively, is something that
Affymetrix decided to do.  To the best of my understanding, the rule
that Affymetrix used to label the alleles A or B is as follows:

Allele pair on the sense strand => AB label
AC => AB
AG => AB
AT => AB
CG => AB
CT => AB
GT => AB

For example, if the allele nucleotides on the sense strands are C and
G, getting an genotype call BB will translate back to GG.  In other
words, you have to know the what the possible allele nucleotides are
to map the (A/B) genotype back to a (A,C,G,T) genotype, and that
information you'll find in the CDF file.  One could imaging the
genotyping tools do this for you, but they normally don't because the
actually nucleotide is less of interest.

Is this what you are looking for?

/Henrik

>
>
>  Thanks and Best,
>
>  R
>
>  >
>

messages.subject: Ensembl49 gene-based CDF now available
messages.body_plain:
Hi all.

I have now created an Ensembl CDF based on the newly released Ensembl
49 human build.  They can be downloaded from:

http://bioinf.wehi.edu.au/folders/mrobinson/exon/human_cdfs/
(HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl49,G-Affy.cdf)

I've update the google groups page:
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/ensembl-gene-
defintions

For those counting, there are ~1800 less units in the Ensembl 49
version and that is simply because I have applied a filter to the
'Biotype' column in the Biomart query.  See below.  I've now only
included 'protein_coding' and 'pseudogene'.  Anyone have a
preference?  If so, I can easily change.

Cheers,
Mark

(Ensembl 49 CDF totals)

unix88 543 %  awk '{FS="\t"; print $3}' mart_export.txt | sort | uniq -c
  270616 protein_coding
    4527 pseudogene

(Ensembl 47 CDF totals)

unix88 542 %  awk '{FS="\t"; print $3}' martquery_1116012517_968.txt
| sort | uniq -c
     102 C_segment
      32 D_segment
      99 J_segment
  274280 protein_coding
    4660 pseudogene
    1018 repeat
     565 retrotransposed
     334 rRNA
     471 V_segment

always frustrating to fix it when it's loaded in the wrong order. I
haven't tried it yet...

Elizabeth

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

As a beginner, I copied some code (see the following)
and did the preprocessing for my exon arrays.  But I
do not know how to intepret those normalized files.
Here are my specific questions:

As you see in the following code, I generated two
files, one is to merge all the exon probe sets  and
get an overall gene expression level for a transcript
cluster ID, that is the file "plmCore.BrCL.txt" and it
has 18708 rows; another is to NOT merge those exon
probe sets, file name is "plmCoreBrCL.NoMerge.txt",
and I got 284258 rows. My goal is to map those exon
probe sets and transcript cluster ID to official gene
symbols (e.g. genes MYOD1, PR, ER and so on) for my
further analysis. How can I do that?  I know how to do
this for affymetrix U133 data, but for the exon array
data I do not know how to extract the gene ID (or
transcript ID) information from the affy CDF file
and/or annotation file. I searched UCSC genome browser
web and found one file (named "affyHumanExon.txt") in
their annotation directory, but I am not sure how will
that help. I searched in this aroma.affymetrix group
list, did  not  find exact answer. Any feedback is
helpful.

 Thanks! and here is my code:

library(aroma.affymetrix)

verbose<-Arguments$getVerbose(-8)
timestampOn(verbose)

chipType <- "HuEx-1_0-st-v2"
cdf <-
AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("HuEx-1_0-st-v2")
print(cdf)

# cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType,
tags="core")
# print(cdf)

cdfCore<-AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(paste(chipType,"coreR3,A20071112,EP",sep=","))
BC.exon <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name=name,
chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2" )
setCdf(BC.exon, cdfCore)

bc<-RmaBackgroundCorrection(BC.exon)
system.time(process.bc<-process(bc, verbose=verbose) )
# How come it works in my laptop, but not bilbo, is it
becasue the version of R there is not correct?

#quantile normalization:
BcExon.quan <- QuantileNormalization(process.bc,
typesToUpdate="pm",tags=c("*"))
process.BcExon.quan <- process(BcExon.quan,
verbose=verbose,force=F)
# takes about 30 to 40 minutes

#RMA model fitting:
#----
#Fit to core transcript clusters
#----

setCdf(BC.exon, cdfCore)
plmCore.BrCL <- ExonRmaPlm(process.BcExon.quan ,
mergeGroups=TRUE,tags=c("*","core"))
fit(plmCore.BrCL, verbose=verbose)
# About 50 minutes in my laptop
#----
#Fit to core probesets
#----

setCdf(BC.exon, cdfCore)
plmCoreBrCL.NoMerge <- ExonRmaPlm(process.BcExon.quan,
mergeGroups=FALSE,tags=c("*","core"))
fit(plmCoreBrCL.NoMerge, verbose=verbose)
# take about 70 minutes

#----------------- output
celNames <- paste(getNames(BC.exon),".CEL",sep="");
header <- t(c("Probeset", celNames));

ces<-getChipEffectSet(plmCoreBrCL.NoMerge);
pbsetSumm<-extractMatrix(ces,returnUgcMap=TRUE,units=NULL);
# pbsetSumm<-log2(pbsetSumm);
 pbsetSumm<-round(log2(pbsetSumm), 3) ; # Mar 31,
notes, to save space, here I only save 3 digits
pbsetNames<-readCdfGroupNames(getPathname(getCdf(ces)),unit=NULL,truncate=F)
rownames(pbsetSumm)<-unlist(pbsetNames)
write.table(header, file="plmCoreBrCL.NoMerge.txt",
sep="\t", quote=FALSE, row.names=FALSE,
col.names=FALSE);
write.table(pbsetSumm, file="plmCoreBrCL.NoMerge.txt",
sep="\t", quote=FALSE, append=TRUE, row.names=TRUE,
col.names=FALSE);

ces<-getChipEffectSet(plmCore.BrCL);
pbsetSumm<-extractMatrix(ces,returnUgcMap=TRUE,units=NULL);
# pbsetSumm<-log2(pbsetSumm);
pbsetSumm<-round(log2(pbsetSumm), 3) ;  # Mar 31,
notes, to save space, here I only save 3 digits
pbsetNames<-readCdfGroupNames(getPathname(getCdf(ces)),unit=NULL,truncate=F)
rownames(pbsetSumm)<-names(pbsetNames)
write.table(header, file="plmCore.BrCL.txt", sep="\t",
quote=FALSE, row.names=FALSE, col.names=FALSE);
write.table(pbsetSumm, file="plmCore.BrCL.txt",
sep="\t", quote=FALSE, append=TRUE, row.names=TRUE,
col.names=FALSE);
save.image()

      ____________________________________________________________________________________

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Questions about annotations
messages.body_plain:
Hi Shuying,

So for your main question -- how to get a gene name for a transcript
cluster id -- you will probably need to use the Affymetrix annotation
for this, regardless of any flaws it might have. See their support pages
for files with names like HuEx-1_0-st-v2.na24.hg18.transcript.csv. While
I'm sure there are many solutions, I don't know of any other
*straight-forward* mapping. However, I am not familiar with what the
Genome Browser is providing these days.

If you are only working with the 25% of the array that make up the core
probesets (so I assume you just want the well-annotated genome and don't
want to search the extended and full probesets) you could instead try
the Ensembl cdf that Mark has created -- he has matched the Affy
probesets to the Ensembl gene/transcript annotation. This has the
advantage that you can take the unit name which is the Ensembl id (e.g.
ENSG00000136527) and then use biomaRt package in R to get the gene name.
Furthermore, Steffen Durinck has created a nice package that (among
other things) allow you to plot data from the exon array against the
transcript information in Ensembl. It will be released on bioconductor
soon. Moreover, genes with overlap are dealt with slightly differently
than Affymetrix, so I think there is less combining of separate genes
into one 'gene'. So there are a lot of advantages to using this cdf.
However, it will not give you a way to extend your analysis to the other
75%(!) of the chip that are not included.

Another, more specific comment regarding your code. The *much* better
way to get the unit/group names to match the output of the extractMatrix
command is to use extractDataFrame() command which has the (non-default)
option to return the unit(gene) and group(exon) names.

Best,
Elizabeth

Hi, I will take the freedom to forward this question to the mailing
list.  Please send *all* questions to the mailing list, because...

"FAQ. 2008-03-26: Why do you not want to answer questions sent to your
private email address?

A: Please post all questions related to aroma.affymetrix to the
aroma-af...@googlegroups.com mailing list.  This way there is a
chance that others also can help out with your problem/question, which
means that you hopefully get a reply quicker.  All questions and
answers are archived and searchable online.  Because of this, we can
then refer to already answered questions by replying with a link.
Moreover, this way the chances for finding answers online increase.
So, please understand this when I ask you to repost your question to
the mailing list.  It will not only save me but everyone a lot of
time."

URL: http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/frequently-asked-questions

More comments below...

On Tue, Apr 1, 2008 at 11:11 AM, Gao Zhang <gzh...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Dr.Bengtsson,
>
> Hi! I am following the thread on the page of
> http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis
>  for set-up.
>
> My affy data is of Affy 250K Sty type so I figured I should put:
>
> Mapping250K_Sty.cdf
> Mapping250K_Sty,na24,HB20080214.ugp, and
> Mapping250K_Sty,na24,HB20080214.ufl
>
> in the folder called 'annotationData/chipTypes/Mapping250K_Sty'.
>
> But I did not find the folder of 'chipTypes' under the 'annotationData'.
> Should
> I manually create these folders? I found the folder 'annotationData' as the
> path of:
>
> C:\Program Files\R\R-2.6.2\library\aroma.affymetrix\annotationData
>
> Please direct me how to do this. I am new to R so sorry for these naive
> questions.

Yes, you have to create those directories yourself.

[The annotationData/ is created as a "side effect" when
aroma.affymetrix tries to locate it and it does not exist.]

Also, you do *not* want to have:

  C:\Program Files\R\R-2.6.2\library\aroma.affymetrix\

as your working directory (trust me on that one).  Instead, make sure
to use another working directory, e.g. under 'C:/...../My
Documents/AffymetrixAnalysis/' in which you create directories (with
subdirectories):

  annotationData/
  rawData/

Then you can use setwd() in your script to set the working directory
to be C:/...../My Documents/AffymetrixAnalysis/.

Cheers

/Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On Tue, Apr 1, 2008 at 6:40 PM,  <GZh...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>  Henrik,
>
>  Are you referring me to look at 'Calculating raw total copy numbers
>  manually' in the vignettes?

I was mainly thinking of the 'Total copy number analysis (10K, 100K,
500K)' vignette which is for the 500K platform you are using.

>  I am wondering whether there is a way to specify two groups of test
>  and reference samples
>  respectively before normalization.

I see.  No, there is no automatic feature in aroma.affymetrix that
allows you to  tag samples "normal" and "non-normal" so that all
downstream methods are aware of this difference and deals with it
specifically.

There are basically two ways to deal with the problem of heterogeneity
of samples:

1) Assume that the majority of your samples are normal (diploid) at
any random locus and rely on the robustness of the estimators not to
be biased by outliers (CN aberrations).
2) Estimate the normalization functions "manually" on the normal
samples only and then apply the fitted function to all samples.

Please see thread 'quantile normalization target distribution' on
March 1, 2008 [ http://tinyurl.com/2rag8x ] on how to do this.  You
basically have to setup an AffymetrixCelSet that contains only your
normal samples and then estimate the target distribution from this
one.  You can then specify to use that distribution when you setup
your QuantileNormalization method.  [I'll see if I can simplify this
process slightly in a future release, but for now, please see the
about thread].

Cheers

/Henrik

On Tue, Apr 1, 2008 at 9:46 PM,  <GZh...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>  Thanks Henrik. I am looking over the 'Total copy number analysis (10K,
>  100K, 500K)'
>  and wondering what are the paths for two folders named
>  'annotationData' and 'rawData'
>  shown in the example. Are they under the same directory?
>
>  I basically wanted to try the code below:
>
>  verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8)
>  timestampOn(verbose)
>  name <- "AGRF_2007a"
>  chipTypes <- c("Mapping250K_Sty")
>  cdfs <- lapply(chipTypes, FUN=function(chipType) {AffymetrixCdfFile
>  $fromChipType(chipType)})
>
>  But I ended up getting:
>
>  > cdfs <- lapply(chipTypes, FUN=function(chipType) {AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType)})
>  Error in list("lapply(chipTypes, FUN = function(chipType) {" =
>  <environment>,  :
>
>  [2008-04-02 00:40:07] Exception: Could not create AffymetrixCdfFile
>  object. No CDF file with that chip type found: Mapping250K_Sty
>   at throw(Exception(...))
>   at throw.default("Could not create ", class(static)[1], " object. No
>  CDF file
>   at throw("Could not create ", class(static)[1], " object. No CDF
>  file with tha
>   at byChipType.AffymetrixCdfFile(static, ...)
>   at byChipType(static, ...)
>   at method(static, ...)
>   at AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType)
>   at FUN("Mapping250K_Sty"[[1]], ...)
>   at lapply.default(chipTypes, FUN = function(chipType) {
>   at lapply(chipTypes, FUN = function(chipType) {
>
>  I put the three annotation files in the folder:
>
>  annotationData/chipTypes/Mapping250K_Sty/
>
>  and a test .cel file in the folder:
>
>  annotationData/rawData/AGRF_2007a/Mapping250K_Sty/

No, the rawData/ directory should not be under annoationData/.  Please
read the 'User Guide' at:

  http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/users-guide

that explains how to setup the directories and where to put what
files, especially the first three sections.  Also, it is *most
important* that you understand what "current working directory" means
and how to get and set this in R, cf. help(setwd).

/Henrik

>
>  Thanks much,
>
>  Alex
>
>
>  On Apr 1, 9:56 pm, "Henrik Bengtsson" <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
>  > Hi.
>  >
>
>
> > On Tue, Apr 1, 2008 at 6:40 PM,  <GZha...@gmail.com> wrote:
>  >
>  > >  Henrik,
>  >
>  > >  Are you referring me to look at 'Calculating raw total copy numbers
>  > >  manually' in the vignettes?
>  >
>  > I was mainly thinking of the 'Total copy number analysis (10K, 100K,
>  > 500K)' vignette which is for the 500K platform you are using.
>  >
>  > >  I am wondering whether there is a way to specify two groups of test
>  > >  and reference samples
>  > >  respectively before normalization.
>  >
>  > I see.  No, there is no automatic feature in aroma.affymetrix that
>  > allows you to  tag samples "normal" and "non-normal" so that all
>  > downstream methods are aware of this difference and deals with it
>  > specifically.
>  >
>  > There are basically two ways to deal with the problem of heterogeneity
>  > of samples:
>  >
>  > 1) Assume that the majority of your samples are normal (diploid) at
>  > any random locus and rely on the robustness of the estimators not to
>  > be biased by outliers (CN aberrations).
>  > 2) Estimate the normalization functions "manually" on the normal
>  > samples only and then apply the fitted function to all samples.
>  >
>  > Please see thread 'quantile normalization target distribution' on
>  > March 1, 2008 [http://tinyurl.com/2rag8x] on how to do this.  You
>  > basically have to setup an AffymetrixCelSet that contains only your
>  > normal samples and then estimate the target distribution from this
>  > one.  You can then specify to use that distribution when you setup
>  > your QuantileNormalization method.  [I'll see if I can simplify this
>  > process slightly in a future release, but for now, please see the
>  > about thread].
>  >
>  > Cheers
>  >
>  > /Henrik
>  >
>  >
>  >
>  > >  Thanks,
>  > >      Alex
>  >
>  > >  On Apr 1, 7:33 pm, "Henrik Bengtsson" <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
>  > >  > Hi.
>  >
>  > > > On Tue, Apr 1, 2008 at 3:39 PM,  <GZha...@gmail.com> wrote:
>  >
>  > >  > >  Hi,
>  >
>  > >  > >  I am wondering whether I can do unpaired total copy number
>  > >  > >  analysis (49 tumor samples and 137 normal samples) using
>  > >  > >  aroma.affymetrix package.
>  >
>  > >  > Yes. Please see online vignettes.
>  >
>  > >  > /Henrik
>  >
>  > >  > >  Thank you very much!
>  >
>  > >  > >  Alex
>  >
>

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Henrik. I also figured that out and it is all good now.
I tried to test the code in the page for 'Total copy number analysis
(10K, 100K, 500K)'
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis

So far so good but except for the code:

rs <- calculateResiduals(plm, verbose=verbose)

The error message was:

> rs <- calculateResiduals(plm, verbose=verbose)
Error in list("calculateResiduals(plm, verbose = verbose)" =
<environment>,  :

[2008-04-02 01:29:34] Exception: calculateResiduals() does not yet
support chip effects for which allele A and allele B have been
combined.
  at throw(Exception(...))
  at throw.default("calculateResiduals() does not yet support chip
effects for w
  at throw("calculateResiduals() does not yet support chip effects for
which all
  at calculateResidualSet.ProbeLevelModel(this, ...)
  at calculateResidualSet(this, ...)
  at calculateResiduals.ProbeLevelModel(plm, verbose = verbose)
  at calculateResiduals(plm, verbose = verbose)

Any suggestions to correct this?

Thanks,
     Alex

The code I used is:

library(aroma.affymetrix)

verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8)
timestampOn(verbose)
name <- "AGRF_2007a"
chipTypes <- c("Mapping250K_Sty")
cdfs <- lapply(chipTypes, FUN=function(chipType) {AffymetrixCdfFile
$fromChipType(chipType)})

print(cdfs)
gis <- lapply(cdfs, getGenomeInformation)
print(gis)
sis <- lapply(cdfs, getSnpInformation)
print(sis)

cesNList <- list()
chipType <- chipTypes[1]
cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chipType)
cs <- extract(cs, !isDuplicated(cs))
print(cs)

qn <- QuantileNormalization(cs)
print(qn)

csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose)

plm <- RmaCnPlm(csN, combineAlleles=TRUE, mergeStrands=TRUE)
print(plm)

fit(plm, verbose=verbose)

rs <- calculateResiduals(plm, verbose=verbose)

messages.subject: Re: bug hunt in CDF
messages.body_plain:
Alistair.

I've copied this to the aroma.affymetrix google group, in case someone else has this problem.

I *think* the CDF is ok.  I don't get this error.

I think the problem is that you have processed (BG adjusted, quantile normalized) the data previously with a different CDF and then try to invoke a PLM, where it first looks for unestimated units ... and there it finds that the number of probes doesn't match.

Two things to do ....

1. use force=TRUE in your 'fit' and 'process' calls ... that will start from scratch and overwrite the CEL files for the normalized data, chip effects, etc.

2. use tags ... with tags, you can process the same dataset with a bunch of different CDFs ... for example, the code below does BG adjustment, normalization on the 'main' set of probesets, but then does fits on the Ensembl 47 or 49 and stores the results in separate locations ...

# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
# setup dataset and chip names
# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
projectName <- "colon_affy"
chipType <- "HuEx-1_0-st-v2"

# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
# define CDF files (main + ensembl)
# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
cdfMain <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(paste(chipType, "main,A20070914,EP", sep=","))
cdfEnsb47 <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(paste(chipType, "U-Ensembl47,G-Affy", sep=","))
cdfEnsb49 <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(paste(chipType, "U-Ensembl49,G-Affy", sep=","))
csColon <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(projectName, chipType=chipType)
setCdf(csColon, cdfMain)

# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
# background correction + quantile normalization
# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
bcColon <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(csColon,tag=c("*","main"),addJitter=T)
csBCColon <- process(bcColon,verbose=verbose)
qnColon <- QuantileNormalization(csBCColon, typesToUpdate="pm")
csNColon <- process(qnColon,verbose=verbose)

# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
# fit probe level models
# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
setCdf(csNColon, cdfEnsb49)
plmColon <- ExonRmaPlm(csNColon, mergeGroups=TRUE,tag=c("*","ens49"))
fit(plmColon, verbose=verbose)
setCdf(csNColon, cdfEnsb47)
plmColon <- ExonRmaPlm(csNColon, mergeGroups=TRUE,tag=c("*","ens47"))
fit(plmColon, verbose=verbose)

.... this will fit PLMs based on both CDFs and you could then go and read chip effects separately .... note that under the hood this will store data in the following directories for:

drwxr-x---  3 mrobinson lab0605 4096 Apr  1 10:41 colon_affy,RBC,main,QN

Let me know if that doesn't work.

Cheers,
Mark

both.  There is no need to do 1 unless you really want to overwrite
your previous analysis.  #2 is probably the preferred since it gives
you more flexibility (i.e. of running separate analysis and not
overwriting anything).

Mark

filePath() is defined in R.utils. If you look at its code you'll find
that it uses readWindowsShortcut(), which is in the same package, to
actually parse the link file.

not break anything on other file systems/OSs.

messages.subject: aroma.affymetrix v0.9.1 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

aroma.affymetrix v0.9.1 is available.  It mainly contains several bug
fixes and other problem reported here.  As for previous updates, more
validation and better error reports have been added in order to
minimize the risk for user and coding mistakes.  This version has been
verified to pass all our redundancy tests.  Please update by:

source("http://www.braju.com/R/hbLite.R")
hbInstall("aroma.affymetrix")

Previously installed patches will automatically be deleted.

Here is a more detailed list of updates:

Version: 0.9.1 [2008-04-04]
o Now setCdf() also reports on the two incompatible chip types involved
  if trying to set a CDF that is not compatible with a CEL file.
o Added getMainCdf() for AffymetrixCdfFile for retrieving the
  "main" CDF given a monocell CDF.
o Now the standard deviation across all CNs in a chromosome is calculated
  using a robust first-order difference estimator, which will make the
  estimate much less affected by copy-number changes.
o BUG FIX: The ArrayExplorer would generate image files to a directory
  under reports/<dataSet>/<tags>,<tags>/..., i.e. the tags where
  replicated.  This is a bug introduced in the latest release.  Thanks
  to
o BUG FIX: getTableOfArrays() of AffymetrixCelSetTuple returned the
  incorrect array indices for the 2nd chip type if different arrays
  in the two sets.
o BUG FIX: Regular expression pattern 'a-Z' is illegal on (at least)
  some locale, e.g. 'C' (where 'A-z' works). The only way to specify
  the ASCII alphabet is to list all characters explicitly, which we now
  do in all methods of the package.  See the r-devel thread
  "invalid regular expression '[a-Z]'" on 2008-03-05 for details.
o BUG FIX: extractMatrix(..., cells=NULL), the default, would throw
  'Error in order(cells) : argument 1 is not a vector'.
o BUG FIX: getUnitIntensities() would not pass arguments '...', e.g.
  'stratifyBy', to readUnits() for AffymetrixCdfFile.  Thanks to
  Tim Keighley, CSIRO, Sydney, for reporting this.
o BUG FIX: Calling readUnits() of an AffymetrixCdfFile without specifying
  the 'units' argument gave an error.  Thanks again Tim Keighley.
o BUG FIX: Calling readUnits(..., units=cdfUnits, stratifyBy=stratifyBy)
  twice with different 'stratifyBy' arguments and with a 'cdfUnits' list
  structure containing the identical set of unit names, would cause
  readUnits() to incorrectly return cached results from the previous call.
o CLEAN UP: Removed the backward compatibility patch from 2007-01-10 that
  made fromDataFile() of ChipEffectFile to add missing tags. If anyone
  still has such old chip effect files lying around, they have to either
  add the tags manually or reanalyze the data if they want the fullnames
  of the chip effect files to match the fullnames raw data files.
o BETA: Added estimateSds() to CopyNumberChromosomalModel for estimating
  the standard deviation of the raw CNs (log2-ratios) robustly and so
  that change points have minimal impact. This is done by using a
  first-order difference variance estimator.  The reading of the data
  can definitely be made faster, but at least it works for now.  Added
  redundancy tests for this based on the 10K and the 100K chip types.
o BETA: Added static method allocateFromCdf() for AffymetrixCelFile.
o BETA: Added readDataFrame() for AffymetrixCdfFile (SLOOOOW! but will
  be faster when the underlying function in 'affxparser' is updated).
o BETA: Added getUnitGroupCellChromosomePositionMap() to both
  AffymetrixCdfFile and ChipEffectFile.
o BETA: Added isUnitGroupCellMap().
o BETA: Added matrixBlockPolish().

Cheers

/Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jay,
If you use extractDataFrame() on your chip effects, you can ask for this
information to be included (addNames=T). Or you can get this information
from the cdf; for example,

cdfEnsbMono<-AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(paste("HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl47,G-Affy",
"monocell",sep=","))
ugcMapEnsb<-getUnitGroupCellMap(cdfEnsbMono)
ugNamesEnsb <- getUnitGroupNamesFromUgcMap(cdfEnsbMono,ugcMapEnsb)

Then ugNamesEnsb will have this information. This can take a long time
(many minutes) the first time -- but not impossible, I ran it on my
laptop. If you just want a few units, you can also give that as an
option to getUnitGroupCellMap(). This is assuming you have already run
your plm so that you have a 'monocell' version of the Ensembl cdf (which
is created during the fitting process if it doesn't already exist; you
can check in you annotationData folder to see if it's there)

Best,
Elizabeth

> file on 2008-02-14.  dChip "tags" the annotation files with the genome
> build instead, e.g. 'hg18'.  In other words, it is a bit ambiguous
> what NetAffx version dChip use, but my best guess is that Cheng Li
> updates the annotation files quarterly when NetAffx get updated.

> In summary, my best guess is that any differences are only minor and

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: reference in cbs method
messages.body_plain:
Henrik Bengtsson escribió:
> Hi.
>
> On Fri, Mar 14, 2008 at 1:11 PM, vesp...@inmegen.gob.mx
> <vesp...@inmegen.gob.mx> wrote:
>
>>  Henrik Bengtsson escribió:
>>
>>
>>
>>> Hi.
>>>
>>  >
>>  > On Thu, Mar 13, 2008 at 12:25 PM, vesp...@inmegen.gob.mx
>>  > <vesp...@inmegen.gob.mx> wrote:
>>  >
>>  >>  Henrik Bengtsson escribió:
>>  >>
>>  >>
>>  >>
>>  >>> Hi Valeria,
>>  >>>
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  > On Feb 19, 2008 12:52 PM, vesp...@inmegen.gob.mx
>>  >>  > <vesp...@inmegen.gob.mx> wrote:
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  >> Hi,
>>  >>  >>
>>  >>  >> Can someone tell me if it is possible to access the common reference
>>  >>  >> file created and used during the cbs method. Is it possible to use it as
>>  >>  >> a reference in  an other  data set?
>>  >>  >>
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  > Example:
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  > seg <- CbsModel(cesFln);
>>  >>  > fit(seg, chromosome=22);
>>  >>  > refTuple <- getReferenceSetTuple(seg);
>>  >>  > refSet <- getListOfSets(refTuple)[[1]];
>>  >>  > refFile <- getFile(refSet, 1);
>>  >>  > yRef <- getData(refFile, fields="intensities")$intensities;
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  > The above applies to any segmentation method, e.g. GladModel and CbsModel.
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  > Explanation: all segmentation models in aroma.affymetrix can combine
>>  >>  > data from multiple chip types.  The working term for a *list* of CEL
>>  >>  > sets is a *CEL set tuple*.  For each chip type there is a reference,
>>  >>  > either a single file or a set of files.  In the case of a single file,
>>  >>  > we still consider the reference as a set of files (the same file
>>  >>  > replicated multiple times).  So,
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  >   refTuple <- getReferenceSetTuple(glad)
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  > first extract the tuple of CEL set references (contains one or more
>>  >>  > CEL sets).  Since we know there is only one, we extract that one:
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  >   refSet <- getListOfSets(refTuple)[[1]]
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  > This is a (Cn)ChipEffectSet.  In the above case, it contains the same
>>  >>  > reference file replicated nbrOfArrays(cesFln) times.  We get this by:
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  >   refFile <- getFile(refSet, 1)
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  > This is a (Cn)ChipEffectFile, e.g.
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  >> refFile
>>  >>  >>
>>  >>  > CnChipEffectFile:
>>  >>  > Name: .average-intensities-median-mad
>>  >>  > Tags: 01ecc75622a8ca3d584335148e1465cd
>>  >>  > Pathname: plmData/Jeremy_2007-10k,ACC,-XY,RMA,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY/Mapping10K_Xba142
>>  >>  > /.average-intensities-median-mad,01ecc75622a8ca3d584335148e1465cd.CEL
>>  >>  > File size: 445.83kB
>>  >>  > RAM: 0.01MB
>>  >>  > File format: v4 (binary; XDA)
>>  >>  > Chip type: Mapping10K_Xba142,monocell
>>  >>  > Timestamp: 2008-01-24 20:10:47
>>  >>  > Parameters: (probeModel: chr "pm", mergeStrands: logi TRUE, combineAlleles: logi
>>  >>  >  TRUE)
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  > As you see, it is actually a regular CEL file, but hidden away and
>>  >>  > with a hashcode part of the filename.
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  > The best way to get the probe signals is (for now):
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  >   yRef <- getData(refFile, fields="intensities")$intensities
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  > Hope this helps
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  > /Henrik
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  >> Thanks!
>>  >>  >> Valeria
>>  >>  >>
>>  >>  >>
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  > >
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  >
>>  >>  Thank you Henrik.
>>  >>  Is there an instruction that allows you to generate the reference cel
>>  >>  file without doing the segmentation?
>>  >>
>>  >
>>  > See online Vignette 'Calculating Raw Total Copy Numbers Manually'.
>>  > Those instructions does not tell you how to deal with XX and XY for
>>  > ChrX.  That you have to do yourself.
>>  >
>>  >
>>  >>  And, is there an instruction that allows you to select a subgroup from
>>  >>  the original data set to calculate the reference and then use it to do
>>  >>  the segmentation of the whole data set?
>>  >>
>>  >
>>  > The GladModel and the CbsModel can be subseted to fit a single
>>  > chromosome (and a single) array, but you cannot subset to a particular
>>  > region.
>>  >
>>  > Alternatively, see the above vignette for estimating raw CNs on a
>>  > subset.  To run segmentation on those, you have to call the GLAD or
>>  > the CBS methods (in the corresponding packages) manually.  That's
>>  > beyond the scope of aroma.affymetrix.
>>  >
>>  > Hope this helps
>>  >
>>  > Henrik
>>  >
>>  >
>>  >>
>>  >>  >
>>  >>
>>  >>
>>  >
>>  > >
>>  >
>>  >
>>  Hi Henrik,
>>
>>  I think I didn't explain myself last time.
>>  What I want to know is if there is a way to select a subset of samples
>>  to be the reference set. In other words, Is it possible to obtain the
>>  robust average across a subset of samples instead of the robust avarage
>>  across all samples? I know a way to do this would be to create a
>>  subdirectory in rawData that only contains the subset and from there
>>  obtain the reference but is there a more efficient way to do this?
>>
>
> You don't have to do this.  You can grab a subset of the samples/files
> from a set using the extract() method and calculate the robust average
> of those, e.g.
>
> cesRef <- extract(ces, c(1:3, 8:11, 34));  A CnChipEffectSet
> ceRef <- getAverageFile(cesRref);  # A CnChipEffectFile
> rm(cesRef);  # Not needed anymore
> print(ceRef);
>
> The you want to use 'ceRef' as you reference in your CBS model.
> Currently (I think) you have to make that single ceRef file into a set
> of (indentical) files of the same size/length as your test set, e.g.
>
> nbrOfArrays <- nbrOfArrays(ces);
> cesRef <- rep(list(ceRef), nbrOfArrays);  # Becomes a list of CnChipEffectFile:s
> cesRef <- newInstance(ces, cesRef);  # Turn it into a set of same type as 'ces'.
>
> cns <- CbsModel(ces, cesRef);
> print(cns);
>
> This is the same idea as when you do paired CN analysis, cf. Vignette
> 'Paired total copy number analysis'.   Now, this becomes a bit more
> complicated if you want to do if for two chip types together, e.g.
> Mapping250K_Nsp and Mapping250K_Sty.  If you want that, first try it
> with one chip type and get it to work, then get back here.
>
> /Henrik
>
>
>>  Thank you,
>>  Valeria
>>
>>
>>
>>  >
>>
>>
>
> >
>
>

>>>  >>  >>
>>>  >>  >> Can someone tell me if it is possible to access the common reference
>>>  >>  >> file created and used during the cbs method. Is it possible to use it as
>>>  >>  >> a reference in  an other  data set?
>>>  >>  >>
>>>  >>  >
>>>  >>  > Example:
>>>  >>  >
>>>  >>  > seg <- CbsModel(cesFln);
>>>  >>  > fit(seg, chromosome=22);
>>>  >>  > refTuple <- getReferenceSetTuple(seg);
>>>  >>  > refSet <- getListOfSets(refTuple)[[1]];
>>>  >>  > refFile <- getFile(refSet, 1);
>>>  >>  > yRef <- getData(refFile, fields="intensities")$intensities;
>>>  >>  >
>>>  >>  > The above applies to any segmentation method, e.g. GladModel and CbsModel.
>>>  >>  >
>>>  >>  > Explanation: all segmentation models in aroma.affymetrix can combine
>>>  >>  > data from multiple chip types.  The working term for a *list* of CEL
>>>  >>  > sets is a *CEL set tuple*.  For each chip type there is a reference,
>>>  >>  > either a single file or a set of files.  In the case of a single file,
>>>  >>  > we still consider the reference as a set of files (the same file
>>>  >>  > replicated multiple times).  So,
>>>  >>  >
>>>  >>  >   refTuple <- getReferenceSetTuple(glad)
>>>  >>  >
>>>  >>  > first extract the tuple of CEL set references (contains one or more
>>>  >>  > CEL sets).  Since we know there is only one, we extract that one:
>>>  >>  >
>>>  >>  >   refSet <- getListOfSets(refTuple)[[1]]
>>>  >>  >
>>>  >>  > This is a (Cn)ChipEffectSet.  In the above case, it contains the same
>>>  >>  > reference file replicated nbrOfArrays(cesFln) times.  We get this by:
>>>  >>  >
>>>  >>  >   refFile <- getFile(refSet, 1)
>>>  >>  >
>>>  >>  > This is a (Cn)ChipEffectFile, e.g.
>>>  >>  >
>>>  >>  >
>>>  >>  >> refFile
>>>  >>  >>
>>>  >>  > CnChipEffectFile:

>>>  >>  > /.average-intensities-median-mad,01ecc75622a8ca3d584335148e1465cd.CEL

>>>  >>  >  TRUE)

>>>  >>  > As you see, it is actually a regular CEL file, but hidden away and
>>>  >>  > with a hashcode part of the filename.
>>>  >>  >
>>>  >>  > The best way to get the probe signals is (for now):
>>>  >>  >
>>>  >>  >   yRef <- getData(refFile, fields="intensities")$intensities
>>>  >>  >
>>>  >>  > Hope this helps

>>>  >>  > /Henrik

>>>  >

>>>  > chromosome (and a single) array, but you cannot subset to a particular
>>>  > region.

>>>  > Alternatively, see the above vignette for estimating raw CNs on a
>>>  > subset.  To run segmentation on those, you have to call the GLAD or
>>>  > the CBS methods (in the corresponding packages) manually.  That's

>>>  robust average across a subset of samples instead of the robust avarage

>> You don't have to do this.  You can grab a subset of the samples/files
>> from a set using the extract() method and calculate the robust average
>> of those, e.g.
>>
>> cesRef <- extract(ces, c(1:3, 8:11, 34));  A CnChipEffectSet
>> ceRef <- getAverageFile(cesRref);  # A CnChipEffectFile
>> rm(cesRef);  # Not needed anymore

>> Currently (I think) you have to make that single ceRef file into a set
>> of (indentical) files of the same size/length as your test set, e.g.
>>
>> nbrOfArrays <- nbrOfArrays(ces);
>> cesRef <- rep(list(ceRef), nbrOfArrays);  # Becomes a list of CnChipEffectFile:s
>> cesRef <- newInstance(ces, cesRef);  # Turn it into a set of same type as 'ces'.
>>
>> cns <- CbsModel(ces, cesRef);
>> print(cns);
>>
>> This is the same idea as when you do paired CN analysis, cf. Vignette
>> 'Paired total copy number analysis'.   Now, this becomes a bit more
>> complicated if you want to do if for two chip types together, e.g.
>> Mapping250K_Nsp and Mapping250K_Sty.  If you want that, first try it
>> with one chip type and get it to work, then get back here.
>>

messages.subject_clean: Parallelizing the Total Copy Number Analysis (GWS6)
messages.body_plain:
In particular, if I understand it correctly, the probe-level
summarization for GWS6 is done for each array independently, which
means that in theory, one could launch an R instance for each array
that is being analyzed. I am currently analyzing 96 GWS6 arrays and
the AvgCnPlm step is taking more than 12-13 hours, this is why I would
like to parallelize this step because there are more arrays to come.

messages.subject: Re: Problem with Fragment Length Normalization
messages.body_plain:
Thanks Henrik, applying the shift you suggested resolved our problem!

Regards,

 John Watkinson

On Mar 29, 6:07 pm, "Henrik Bengtsson" <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
> Hi,
>
> sorry for the delay  - I just had and will have some more busy weeks
> ahead of me.
>
> You seem to have the correct CDF and UFL files for GWS5.
>
> The main problem, as I mentioned earlier, is that the fragment
> information for GWS5 is only partly correct and that causes the
> problem.  I believe that when we get the correct information from
> Affymetrix your problem will go away.  Without the correct annotation
> data, it is be better for you to skip the fragment-length
> normalization step.
>
> However, if you want troubleshoot further, here is what goes on.  When
> you apply the allelic-crosstalk calibration you will introduce a
> fraction of non-positive probe signals (this is because some
> homozygote SNPs have true allele signal zero for one of the alleles,
> and then we add noise, but also because some signals are very close to
> the signal-to-noise levels).  Some of the non-positive signals will
> carry through to the summarized signals, the averaging over 3-4 SNP
> probes lower the fraction, but some still gets through.  For CN probes
> you will also get some non-positive signals.   The fragment-length
> normalization is modeling the data on the log2 scale, meaning
> non-positive signals will be NAs.  This is normally not a problem
> because there should be enough of finite log2 signals to fit the
> effects.  However, for multi-enzyme chip types such as GWS5 and GWS6,
> we stratify on loci exclusively on one enzyme, and because a large
> fraction of loci are on both enzymes we have a smaller pool to fit the
> model.  If you then have NAs in your data, the number of data points
> gets even smaller.   In your case the intersect of valid data points
> and loci exclusively on Enzyme #2 is zero.  I have committed some
> patches allowing you to get more details about the number of
> non-negative signals, valid loci etc.  Do:
>
> library(aroma.affymetrix);
> downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");
>
> Then, when you have defined your FragmentLengthNormalization object:
>
> fcns <- getTargetFunctions(fln, force=TRUE, verbose=-20)
>
> Look at the verbose output, which will give some details.  It might
> reveal that you've got a lot of non-positive chip-effect estimates
> (hope not).
>
> Moreover, there is an option to add a small offset to data before
> taking the log, e.g.
>
> fln <- FragmentLengthNormalization(cs, shift=+200)
> fcns <- getTargetFunctions(fln, force=TRUE, verbose=-20)
>
> That might give you less NAs on the log2 scale.
>
> Cheers
>
> Henrik

Please read the reference listed in the vignette(s), i.e.:

assessment of raw copy numbers at the single locus level,
Bioinformatics 2008. [pmid: 18204055] [doi:
10.1093/bioinformatics/btn016]

It explains what we mean by "raw CNs" and how they are calculated.

I have added a subsection to both CN vignettes with a code example how
to extract the actually raw CNs.

>  of copy-number regions (CNRs)"
>  and "GLAD". What does exactly mean by 'copy-number regions'? Are you

>  abnormal regions"?

Yes.  Please see the help for the GLAD package and the publication for
its model for more details.

>  'cesN' '.

>  'csN' in the page of
>  'Total copy number analysis (10K, 100K, 500K)'.

I use the 'ces' for reffering to a (Cn)ChipEffectSet and 'cs' for an
(Affymetrix)CelSet.  'cesN' is indicating a normalized
CnChipEffectSet.  See Vignette 'Total Copy Number Analysis (5.0 &
6.0)' for an example.  In the Vignette 'Total copy number analysis
(10K, 100K, 500K)' there are two chip types merged so there everything
is put into a 'cesNList' list object.  So, to follow the 'Calculating
raw total copy numbers manually' vignette you obviously have to work
with cesN <- cesNList[["Mapping250K_Nsp"]] and then cesN <-
cesNList[["Mapping250K_Sty"]].

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: UGP and UFL files?
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On Mon, Apr 7, 2008 at 11:48 AM, JP <playb...@yahoo.com> wrote:
>
>  Hi, Henrik, I have a couple of questions regarding to Fragment length
>  calibration.
>
>  (1) The information posted here stating that frangement length effect
>  would be canceled out when computing log2 ratio of two samples. Does
>  that mean fragment length calibration makes no difference when what I
>  need is log2 ratio of each sample to a reference?
>  http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/calibration-and-normalization-of-summarized-data

Where is "here"?

I'm not sure what your question is since you are referring to the page
explaining that we model and correct for the effect on the log2 chip
effect scale (to avoid doing it on log2 ratios which wouldn't allow us
to go back to chip effects afterward).  Fragment-length effects do not
cancel out if they differ between arrays.

>
>  (2) also from the same link as above, what is the current system to
>  track enzymes for each fragment?

Could you please be more precise.  The fragment lengths in the UFL
files are inferred from NetAffx files provided by Affymetrix.

>
>  (3) How the GC content of PCR fragment is calculated by
>  aroma.affymetrix? From what I understood, only length, start and stop
>  positions are required in UFL file.

GC contents is not corrected for in the PCR fragment-length
normalization.  The latter uses the UFL file, which as you say, do not
contain GC-content information.

There is a GcContentNormalization class normalizing CnChipEffectSet:s, e.g.

  gcn <- GcContentNormalization(ces)
  process(gcn, verbose=verbose)

I hardly never do GC-content normalization which is why I haven't
pushed the method nor added major support for the method.  In order
process the above, you will have to download an Affymetrix TSV file
and place it in the corresponding chip-type annotationData/ directory.
 You know you have it working when you can do:

> cdf <- getCdf(ces);
> tsv <- AffymetrixTsvFile$byChipType(getChipType(cdf, fullname=FALSE));
> print(tsv);
AffymetrixTsvFile:
Name: Mapping250K_Sty
Tags:
Pathname: annotationData/chipTypes/Mapping250K_Sty/Mapping250K_Sty.tsv
File size: 9.21MB
RAM: 0.00MB

That is the same code that process(gcn) use.

The Affymetrix TSV file I once got from Affymetrix (cannot remember
where), are ASCII files and are/were used by CNAT v4.  They look like:

> bfr <- readLines(getPathname(tsv), n=5)
[1] "probeset_id\tchr\tsnp_pos\tlen\tGC\tgc_count"
[2] "SNP_A-1780271\t15\t31183071\t625\t35.68\t223"
[3] "SNP_A-1780274\t20\t33371323\t367\t44.959\t165"
[4] "SNP_A-1780277\t12\t73950313\t652\t41.411\t270"
[5] "SNP_A-1780278\t1\t215279053\t682\t35.924\t245"

> cat(bfr, sep="\n")
probeset_id     chr     snp_pos len     GC      gc_count
SNP_A-1780271   15      31183071        625     35.68   223
SNP_A-1780274   20      33371323        367     44.959  165
SNP_A-1780277   12      73950313        652     41.411  270
SNP_A-1780278   1       215279053       682     35.924  245

>
>  (4) I have custom array thus I have to populate my own UFL file. I can
>  creat an annotation file similar (but not identical) to NetAffx CSV
>  annotation files. The questions are what the columns and column-
>  headers required by aroma.affymetrix?

If you already have the data in a convenient data structure in R, it
might be easier for you to just allocated an empty UFL file and
populate it manually:

cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType("Mapping250K_Nsp")
ufl <- AromaUflFile$allocateFromCdf(cdf, tags="na24,JP20080408");

The units (rows) of a UFL are ordered exactly as in the CDF.  So you
have to identify the correct unit index for each unit name, e.g.

> unitNames <- c("SNP_A-1796078", "SNP_A-4250778");
> units <- indexOf(cdf, names=unitNames);
> print(units);
[1] 101 567

Then you can populate it with fragment lengths, e.g.

ufl[units,1] <- c(658, 439)

If you want to proceed by immitating a NetAffx,  please see the
following source code:

print(readDataUnitFragmentLength.AffymetrixNetAffxCsvFile)

/Henrik

>
>  Thanks,
>
>  Jin
>
>
>

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Parallelizing the Total Copy Number Analysis (GWS6)
messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Parallelizing the Total Copy Number Analysis (GWS6)
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On Tue, Apr 8, 2008 at 1:39 PM, Nicolas Stransky
<nicolas....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>  In particular, if I understand it correctly, the probe-level
>  summarization for GWS6 is done for each array independently, which
>  means that in theory, one could launch an R instance for each array
>  that is being analyzed. I am currently analyzing 96 GWS6 arrays and
>  the AvgCnPlm step is taking more than 12-13 hours, this is why I would
>  like to parallelize this step because there are more arrays to come.
>  Has anyone got hints about how to proceed?

First, it is often much faster to work toward a local drive than over
a network file system.  I say this, because quite a few people are one
a shared file system.

Second, about Avg[Cn]Plm: Yes, the underlying model is a single-array
model.  However, due to lack of time, I actually let it inherit from
the ProbelLevelModel class (just like RmaPlm) so that I could reuse
the whole load-fit-save framework.  This means it indeed loads data in
chunks of units across all arrays and then fit the data array by
array.  It is on my lengthy todo list to make this a truly
array-by-array implementation (the estimates will be the same).

Third, before discussing parallelization, there is one obvious thing
one can do to speed up the processing of chip types with single-probe
probeset.  For instance, in GenomeWideSNP_{5|6} all CN units are
single-probe units, but they are still treated as units with unit
groups/probeset in all ways what that means, e.g. loading data in
across arrays wrapped up in a nested list, pass it to the internal fit
function, the unwrap the estimates and store them to file.  This is
done although the chip effect estimates for single-probe probesets are
all identical to probe signals (and there is no across-array
parameters/modelling).  In other words, one can update the
ProbelLevelModel class, and more specifically the fit() method, to
become aware of single-probe units and just "copy and paste" the probe
signals array by array first.  Doing that will probably speed up the
fit() call substantially - probably twice as fast for the GWS5/6
chips.  This is on my todo list as well, but since it is a
low-priority for me, it is unlikely that it will make it up to the top
anytime soon.  You are more than welcome to contribute to this work.
If you do, please let me know.

Fourth, another thing way down on my todo list is to add a
*bullet-proof* and *cross-platform* file-locking mechanism for writing
to files such that "one" has to wait for the file to be release before
writing to it. Next, fit() of ProbeLevelModel need to be updated to
not process the units chunks in order, but in a random order.  With
these two features on can have multiple hosts process the same
PLM/data set at the same time.  Again, contributions are most welcome.
 The file-locking mechanism is something that should be developed and
tested independently of aroma.affymetrix.

/Henrik

>
>  Thank you so much,
>
>
> Nicolas Stransky
>  >
>

messages.subject: Chromosome Explorer
messages.body_plain:
Dear Henrik

I have just computed CN for 168 Sty-arrays using GLAD. This took about
3 days (including normalizations). Chromosome Explorer produced more
than 31,000 figures.

I must say that I like Chromosome Explorer very much, but I have a
couple of questions:

1, Explanation of figures:
a, The middle blue line is equal to log2ratio=0. I assume that the
upper/lower blue lines are the confidence intervals given by the
standard deviation, e.g. sigma=0.213: only black lines outside this
range are considered to be positive. Is this correct?

b, The dots are the raw copy-number values of the SNPs and the crosses
are SNPs considered to be outliers. Is this correct?

2, Names of CEL-files:
The Explorer shows as sample names the names of the CEL-files, which
in my case is e.g. V2443. Since V2443 belongs e.g. to cell line PC3, I
would like to have the real sample names to be displayed, e.g. by
providing a pheno-file table. Is this possible?

Looking at "ChromosomeExplorer.onLoad.js" there is a function
"this.setSampleAliases()" which I suppose may be used for this
purpose. How and at which step do I call this function?

3, Sample+Chromosome+Position:
When opening the browser, is there a possibility to tell the browser
to show a certain sample and a certain chromosome with the figure
moved horizontally thus that the vertical line is shown at the given
position?

The reason for this question is that people are often interested in a
certain sample and gene. Thus it would be great if I could write an R
function where inputs are: "sample name, chromosome, position"
and the output is to open the browser with the defined sample and
position displayed. Is this possible?

4, Gene positions:
Since aroma.affymetrix can also analyze exon-arrays, the optimal
solution would be if the positions of the genes or exons could be
displayed in the figures, too, similar to the Affymetrix GTC browser.
Did you ever consider this possibility?

5, Integration with other browsers:
Is it possible (or do you consider) to integrate the
ChromosomeExplorer into an existing browser, e.g. UCSC-browser or
Ensembl-browser?
Or, alternatively, is it possible to open another browser at the
current region, as the Affymetrix GTC browser does with the UCSC- or
Ensemble-browser?

Thank you in advance.
Best regards
Christian

On 9 avr, 00:56, "Henrik Bengtsson" <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
> Hi.

Hi Henrik,
Thank you for your answer.

> First, it is often much faster to work toward a local drive than over
> a network file system.  I say this, because quite a few people are one
> a shared file system.

Thanks for the advice, I will experiment on this. I am indeed working
on a network filesystem, but it had never been a bottleneck until
now.

> Second, about Avg[Cn]Plm: Yes, the underlying model is a single-array
> model.  However, due to lack of time, I actually let it inherit from
> the ProbelLevelModel class (just like RmaPlm) so that I could reuse
> the whole load-fit-save framework.  This means it indeed loads data in
> chunks of units across all arrays and then fit the data array by
> array.  It is on my lengthy todo list to make this a truly
> array-by-array implementation (the estimates will be the same).

Does this mean that for each array to be fitted, all data from all
arrays has to be read? Indeed I observed that most time was spent
reading and writing data, according to these time summaries:

20080409 09:54:24| Total time for all units across all 96 arrays:
77602.51s == 1293.38min
20080409 09:54:24| Total time per unit across all 96 arrays: 0.04s/
unit
20080409 09:54:24| Total time per unit and array: 0.43ms/unit & array
20080409 09:54:24| Total time for one array (1881415 units): 13.47min
= 0.22h
20080409 09:54:24| Total time for complete data set: 1293.38min =
21.56h
20080409 09:54:24| Fraction of time spent on different tasks: Fitting:
1.0%, Reading: 29.3%, Writing: 68.1% (of which 84.98% is for encoding/
writing chip-effects), Explicit garbage collection: 1.5%

> Third, before discussing parallelization, there is one obvious thing
> one can do to speed up the processing of chip types with single-probe
> probeset.  For instance, in GenomeWideSNP_{5|6} all CN units are
> single-probe units, but they are still treated as units with unit
> groups/probeset in all ways what that means, e.g. loading data in
> across arrays wrapped up in a nested list, pass it to the internal fit
> function, the unwrap the estimates and store them to file.  This is
> done although the chip effect estimates for single-probe probesets are
> all identical to probe signals (and there is no across-array
> parameters/modelling).  In other words, one can update the
> ProbelLevelModel class, and more specifically the fit() method, to
> become aware of single-probe units and just "copy and paste" the probe
> signals array by array first.  Doing that will probably speed up the
> fit() call substantially - probably twice as fast for the GWS5/6
> chips.  This is on my todo list as well, but since it is a
> low-priority for me, it is unlikely that it will make it up to the top
> anytime soon.  You are more than welcome to contribute to this work.
> If you do, please let me know.

I can try to have a look at this once I am more familiar with the
whole implementation but since fitting seems to account for only 1% of
the time I think the issue may not be there in my case :)

> Fourth, another thing way down on my todo list is to add a
> *bullet-proof* and *cross-platform* file-locking mechanism for writing
> to files such that "one" has to wait for the file to be release before
> writing to it. Next, fit() of ProbeLevelModel need to be updated to

>  The file-locking mechanism is something that should be developed and
> tested independently of aroma.affymetrix.

That would help a lot indeed, but I don't think I can do it myself
unfortunately.

Best regards,
Nicolas

Hi,

I have run the Total Copy Number Analysis on 96 SNP6.0 arrays and I
end up with a CnChipEffectSet.

> print(cesN)
CnChipEffectSet:
Name: TRIBE
Tags: ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY

Number of arrays: 96

Time period: 2008-04-08 12:10:06 -- 2008-04-08 12:10:20
Total file size: 2587.13MB
RAM: 0.13MB
Parameters: (probeModel: chr "pm", mergeStrands: logi TRUE,
combineAlleles: logi TRUE)

I'd like to extract all raw copy number values (that is, the signal
after removal of all effects, before segmentation) for all the chips
including normals, in order to export them. What would be the proper
way to do this?
Ideally I don't want to use a common reference before that step
because I don't have case-control pairs of samples and the number of
normal samples will be reduced and may vary from batch to batch so I'd
prefer to use a reference that would be the robust average across
normal samples, once I have extracted the values.

I have seen that it's also possible to run
rawCNs <- extractRawCopyNumbers(cbs, array=1, chromosome=1)
but apparently, the common reference is by default calculated as the
robust average across samples, which is a step I would prefer to deal
with later as explained above.

Thank you so much for your answers,
Nicolas

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Chromosome Explorer
messages.body_plain:
On Wed, Apr 9, 2008 at 1:25 PM, cstratowa
<Christian...@vie.boehringer-ingelheim.com> wrote:
>
>  Dear Henrik
>
>  I have just computed CN for 168 Sty-arrays using GLAD. This took about
>  3 days (including normalizations). Chromosome Explorer produced more
>  than 31,000 figures.
>
>  I must say that I like Chromosome Explorer very much, but I have a
>  couple of questions:
>
>  1, Explanation of figures:
>  a, The middle blue line is equal to log2ratio=0. I assume that the
>  upper/lower blue lines are the confidence intervals given by the
>  standard deviation, e.g. sigma=0.213: only black lines outside this
>  range are considered to be positive. Is this correct?

No, there are no confidence intervals shown.  The upper and lower
lines are just log2(3/2) and log2(1/2); since the CNs are not
calibrated to be proportional to true CN level (typically they are
"compressed") these lines are of little use.

>
>  b, The dots are the raw copy-number values of the SNPs and the crosses
>  are SNPs considered to be outliers. Is this correct?

Yes, assuming that you use the GLAD segmentation model.  Please see
documentation of the GLAD package for further details.

>
>
>  2, Names of CEL-files:
>  The Explorer shows as sample names the names of the CEL-files, which
>  in my case is e.g. V2443. Since V2443 belongs e.g. to cell line PC3, I
>  would like to have the real sample names to be displayed, e.g. by
>  providing a pheno-file table. Is this possible?

If your CEL files have extra tags they will be shown when that array
is displayed.  e.g. in the list of links may be "A01", "A02", "A03"
and then you could see say "Sample: A02 (A02,tagA,tagB)".  Thus, but
add the sample names as tags they can be displayed.

>
>  Looking at "ChromosomeExplorer.onLoad.js" there is a function

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jay,

Without having looked at the source code, I am assuming these are created by a save() or saveObject() call somewhere in the code for process.CbsModel().  XDR is the binary format used by R when saving objects to a file.  (side note: it is not the same as the XDR standard developed by Sun for representing and encoding data, but is based on it and is similar.)  It is probably possible to read these directly into R to see what is stored there, but I would not recommend it as part of a "real" analysis.  If you are intending to try and parse these files outside R you should try searching the R help archive at http://tolstoy.newcastle.edu.au/R/.

Cheers,

Ken

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: xdr files
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

as Ken says, these files are stored using saveObject() [in 'R.utils'],
which essentially is a convenient wrapper around save() [in 'base'].
They contain the R object returned by the segmentation function (e.g.
DNAcopy::segment() and GLAD:glad()).  By saving the results to file
this way, next time you can fit() of the segmentation on the same
chromosome and same array (and with the same segmentation parameters)
the fit can be reloaded from file, which is much faster, especially
for large chromosomes.  You can see the code fit() of the
CopyNumberSegmentationModel class for details.  Please do *not* build
code that rely on these files and this file format, instead call fit()
to retrieve their values.

/Henrik

wrote:

> Hi,
>
> I have run the Total Copy Number Analysis on 96 SNP6.0 arrays and I
> end up with a CnChipEffectSet.
>
> > print(cesN)
>
> CnChipEffectSet:
> Name: TRIBE
> Tags: ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY
> Path: plmData/TRIBE,ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY/GenomeWideSNP_6
> Chip type: GenomeWideSNP_6,Full,monocell
> Number of arrays: 96
> Names: TRIBE_A01_155716, TRIBE_A02_155732, ..., TRIBE_H12_155906
> Time period: 2008-04-08 12:10:06 -- 2008-04-08 12:10:20
> Total file size: 2587.13MB
> RAM: 0.13MB
> Parameters: (probeModel: chr "pm", mergeStrands: logi TRUE,
> combineAlleles: logi TRUE)
>
> I'd like to extract all raw copy number values (that is, the signal
> after removal of all effects, before segmentation) for all the chips
> including normals, in order to export them. What would be the proper
> way to do this?
> Ideally I don't want to use a common reference before that step
> because I don't have case-control pairs of samples and the number of
> normal samples will be reduced and may vary from batch to batch so I'd
> prefer to use a reference that would be the robust average across
> normal samples, once I have extracted the values.
>
> I have seen that it's also possible to run
> rawCNs <- extractRawCopyNumbers(cbs, array=1, chromosome=1)
> but apparently, the common reference is by default calculated as the
> robust average across samples, which is a step I would prefer to deal
> with later as explained above.

In order to to calculate copy numbers you need to have a reference,
i.e. raw CN are defined as log2(theta/thetaR) and you need the
'thetaR' part.  If you only want to extract the 'theta', that is, the
chip effects, you can use extractMatrix() or extractDataFrame(), e.g.

# Identify units on Chr22
cdf <- getCdf(cesN);
gi <- getGenomeInformation(cdf);
units <- getUnitsOnChromosome(gi, 22);

# Extract theta:s for Chr22
theta <- extractTheta(cesN, units=units);

# Extract the same with additional annotation
data <- extractDataFrame(cesN, units=units, addNames=TRUE);

If you use 'units=NULL', all units will be returned.

/Henrik

>
> Thank you so much for your answers,
> Nicolas

messages.subject: We need your help...
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I am glad to report that the the number of aroma.affymetrix users and
the number of installations have grown rapidly over the last few
months, and that this steady growth seems to continue.  Likewise what
happen to other open-source applications when the number of users
increases, more feedback and suggestions are given and more bugs are
found, which over time leads to a higher-quality product.  What also
happens is that more and more questions are asked through the mailing
list.  We (mainly Elizabeth, Mark and Henrik) try our best to answer
these questions promptly.  However, in order to be able to keep up
with this, I would like you to consider the following:

1) Short and precise questions are more likely to be replied to
promptly, simply because they are easier to answer.

2) Have one main question per message.  Avoid putting unrelated
questions in the same message.

3) If you provide as much information as possible about your problem
(e.g. the type of data set, chip type, R script, error message,
sessionInfo() and traceback()), it is easier to locate the problem and
we don't have to spend time asking for such information.  Please put
yourself in the position of the person going to help you.

4) If you see a question that you know the answer to, please feel free
to respond to it.  If you're not 100% sure you get it correct, we can
always pitch in afterward.

These guidelines will save us all (including you) a lot of time and
hopefully we can all focus our resources on what we all like - the
research.  Please note that the development of aroma.affymetrix is
mostly done as a "side" project to our PhD and postdoc projects.

Thanks a lot

Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On Mon, Apr 14, 2008 at 3:49 PM, cstratowa
<Christian...@vie.boehringer-ingelheim.com> wrote:
>
>  Dear Henrik
>

>
>    model <- CbsModel(cesList, refList);
>    ce  <- ChromosomeExplorer(model);
>    tmp <- process(ce);
>    arrays <- indexOfArrays(model);
>    cnrs <- getRegions(model, arrays=arrays);
>
>  or do I need to explicitely do:
>    tmp <- fit(model);
>    cnrs <- getRegions(model, arrays=arrays);

It is enough to do:

model <- CbsModel(cesList, refList);
cnrs <- getRegions(model, arrays=2:3, chromosomes=18:19, verbose=log);

getRegions() will always call fit(), passing the arguments 'arrays'
and 'chromosomes' along, and the "extract" regions from the fit
objects returned by the underlying segmentation method.  This works
for both CbsModel and GladModel.

If you call this twice, you'll find that the fit() will find the
cached results the 2nd time.

>
>
>  2, Zoomx128:
>  Although all images "name,x128.png" are present, both Mozilla and
>  Firefox are only able to display them for chromosomes 7-23, but not
>  for chromosomes 1-6. This problem is not present for Zoom<=64x, only
>  for Zoom=128x. Is this a known issue?

Yes, this is a known issue with Firefox.  Those PNGs are too large for
Firefox to display.  *Hopefully* that the upcoming Firefox v3 will be
able to show these - note, ChromosomeExplorer does currently not work
in Firefox v3.

>
>
>  3, CBS figures:
>  While running ChromosomeExplorer for GLAD resulted in 30,910
>  (=168*23*8) figures, running ChromosomeExplorer for CBS resulted in
>  only 25,208 figures, although I did not get any error message. Do you
>  have a hint what the reason might be?

Since 25208 factors into 137*23*8 (prime factors 137*23*2*2*2) it
looks to me that there are samples for which plots were not generate.
It should be easy to locate which are missing by using Unix ls and
grep or alternatively list.files(pattern, path, recursive=TRUE) in R.

/Henrik

>
>  Best regards
>  Christian

estimate is the MAD of the first-order differences of the raw CNs
across the whole chromosome.  In aroma.affymetrix v0.9.0 and before

the MAD of the raw CNs across the chromosome (not the first-order
difference).

be displayed/generated/saved):

<simpleError in UseMethod("estimateStandardDeviation"): no applicable
method for "estimateStandardDeviation">

if you look at the verbose output.  I've committed a patch - to update do:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix")

You know when it works again if you can do something like:

plot(cbs, array=1, chromosome=19, verbose=-20)

without any errors being displayed.  I have also added a subscript
$\Delta$ to indicate that the estimate is based on the first-order
*differences*.

sigma:s at all for your most recent CbsModel graphs, if you run

messages.body_plain:
I am also attempting to parallelize total copy number analysis of a
large number of GWS5 chips (~1400). However, a file-locking mechanism
sounds like a difficult and involved approach that could retain some
bottlenecks. A workaround in the interim would be to associate a
unique number with each segment (or "sub-job") of the larger job (most
cluster engines make such a number readily available) and then use
this number to ensure that all files written are unique. A "merging"
phase could follow at the end to combine the results in to a single
result. That may be too much to ask of the ChromosomeExplorer, but at
least the regions.xls file could be reconstituted. This cluster step
is probably only needed for the segmentation step, as this is easily
the most time-consuming.

Henrik, do you have any tips as how one could go about introducing
this extra "cluster node number" parameter and propogating it through
to all files written during the segmentation process? As an
experiment, I naively ran the segmentation on a cluster by breaking up
the chips to be processed over 200 nodes. The nodes all had network
file system access to the results of the previous processing steps.
The analysis was successfully completed, but the nodes overwrote each
other's output files.

Thanks in advance for any suggestions.

 John Watkinson

>
> > Third, before discussing parallelization, there is one obvious thing

> > single-probe units, but they are still treated as units with unit

> > fit() call substantially - probably twice as fast for the GWS5/6
> > chips.  This is on my todo list as well, but since it is a
> > low-priority for me, it is unlikely that it will make it up to the top
> > anytime soon.  You are more than welcome to contribute to this work.
> > If you do, please let me know.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I don't understand where the expression

  matrix(data=0, ncol=length(snp.per.gene), nrow=length(snp.per.gene))

It is not in aroma.affymetrix.  When you say you start a new R
session, are you sure you also start without loading a saved image?
Basically, when you start R, make sure you that 'objs' is empty when
you do:

> objs <- ls(all.names=FALSE);
> print(objs);
> str(objs);

Then load aroma.affymetrix and run your script.  Also, what does

> print(summary)

> print(summary.matrix)

give after you get the error message?

/Henrik

messages.subject: Argument mismatch in getUnitsOnChromosome
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

See below for some code that illustrates this (very minor) problem.
Basically, getUnitsOnChromosome.GenomeInformation has an argument
"chromosomes" (plural) while getUnitsAt.AromaUgpFile (called by
getUnitsOnChromosome.UgpGenomeInformation) has an argument "chromosome"
(singular).

> methods(getUnitsOnChromosome)
[1] getUnitsOnChromosome.GenomeInformation
[2] getUnitsOnChromosome.UgpGenomeInformation
> args(getUnitsOnChromosome.GenomeInformation)
function (this, chromosomes, region = NULL, ..., .checkArgs = TRUE)
NULL
> args(getUnitsOnChromosome.UgpGenomeInformation)
function (this, ...)
NULL
> getUnitsOnChromosome.UgpGenomeInformation
function (this, ...)
{
    ugp <- getAromaUgpFile(this)
    getUnitsAt(ugp, ...)
}
attr(,"modifiers")
[1] "public"
> args(getUnitsAt.AromaUgpFile)
function (this, chromosome, region = NULL, ..., verbose = FALSE)
NULL

There are (at least) 2 ways to solve this. You can either change one of
the arguments so they are both either plural or singular, or add a
chromosomes argument to getUnitsOnChromosome.UgpGenomeInformation which
maps to the chromosome argument of getUnitsAt.AromaUgpFile.

Henrik, is there a better way that I should be reporting such minor
problems? I feel bad about spamming the list with simple bug reports.

Cheers,
Tim Keighley

>  the arguments so they are both either plural or singular, or add a
>  chromosomes argument to getUnitsOnChromosome.UgpGenomeInformation which
>  maps to the chromosome argument of getUnitsAt.AromaUgpFile.

Thanks for pointing this out.  I have renamed argument 'chromosome' of
getUnitsAt() for AromaUgpFile to 'chromosomes'.  Install the patches
by:

library(aroma.affymetrix);
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");

FYI, I try to separate arguments in singular and plural so that it is
possible to distinguish between arguments that take scalars and
vectors.  (I have gone through the API to make sure this is true, but
that is the overall strategy).

>
>  Henrik, is there a better way that I should be reporting such minor
>  problems? I feel bad about spamming the list with simple bug reports.

The list *is* the place.  By sending it to the list you: 1) share the
knowledge with others who might have observed the same problem but are
not sure about the reason, 2) make the problem searchable (via say
google), and 3) archive the question/problem.  Setting up a
folder/label filter for mailing lists in email clients is so easy
today that you should never have to worry about filling up peoples
"inboxes".

Cheers

Henrik

>
>  Cheers,
>  Tim Keighley
